**The subject changed.** Moritz, 2026-09-25: *"doing the same great job we did for forward also for
backward ... using what already exists in the tenstorrent repositories. adapting. taking inspiration
from gpu implementations ... full speed. with multiple agents."* Correctness is settled and stays
settled. What is open is speed. **The 58-67x figure (466.70 s against 7-8 s) is SUSPENDED as of
pass 496** — its numerator came off `451ed56f4` and `of3t-stepqb2` now measures the no-exactness
step at **39.886 s** on the current tree, an 11.7x disagreement between two arms that are both
no-exactness (R231). **What does NOT move is the magnitude for the config we actually ship.** The
exactness-ON forward half is measured at **375.908 s** with a DURING clock, so against an H200
*whole* step of 7-8 s that is **~47-54x before the backward is counted at all**. So the collapse
risk is confined to the no-exactness comparison, which was never the shipped configuration; the
shipped gap stays large and its split — **~8.5x compute / ~11x bandwidth is hardware and ~6-7x is
software** — is unaffected, because that split was never derived from the 466.70 s. The sprint
wins the software part or says why it cannot. 5x chip-to-chip is below the silicon floor and this
campaign does not promise it.

**Every J-row on the kernel board is closed, and that is the sprint's main engineering result.**
The premise — that a fused backward kernel is where the backward's time is — is refuted by one
error repeated: `of3t-bwsurvey` ordered the jobs by tape-NODE and verb COUNT, and count does not
track seconds (R211; LayerNorm backward is 52.4 % of nodes and 2.6 % of backward seconds).

**What replaced it was `of3t-xcost`'s attribution — and that has itself been superseded (R250).**
`of3t-stepqb2` measured the backward on a real taped arm: **663.3 s = 432.15 s inside ttnn verbs
(65.15 %) + 231.15 s outside (34.85 %)**, both terms measured. xcost's split below is kept for its
host-price components, which stand, but its **denominator was never measured** — `705.78` is a
literal at `layoutprice.py:143` (R240) — so every share derived from it is off. Reading the
superseded figures (verb self-time, 630.91 s + 74.87 s non-verb = 705.78 s exactly)
the exact softmax on the `[384,4,384,384]` FLOAT32 score block is **437.986 s, 62.06 % of the
backward**, of which only **94.07 s is genuine host float64 arithmetic**: 44.90 s is host
tilize/untilize, 37.66 s an irreducible buffer copy, and **168.51 s is left by subtraction between
DMA, blocking sync and queue drain — three different defects the instrument cannot separate.**
`of3t-xsplit` owns splitting it.

**The sprint's question is answered and that answer is not in dispute.** *Why is the backward
slow?* Because of the fidelity feature we chose, not a missing fused kernel: on a real taped arm
the backward is **663.3 s**, of which **73.5 % of verb time is host crossings** (`to_torch` 178.41
+ `from_torch` 139.13 = 317.54 s) while the model's own arithmetic totals under 2 s and `matmul`
costs **0.85 s over 4,672 calls at 675 GB/s**. The fused-backward-kernel programme the sprint was
premised on is refuted (J1 NO-GO, J2's free route NO-GO, J3 dead at zero, the taped bypass 1.005x),
and `of3t-exactscope` priced the fidelity as non-negotiable rather than narrowable.

PROVES: **OpenFold3's training gradient on Tenstorrent is upstream 0.4.3's gradient to within
upstream's own bf16 error, on every section, over the whole step — stamped pass 444 on `f01fa0813`, AND THAT IS THE TREE IT HOLDS ON, not today's main (R225).** The stamp commit is an ancestor of `origin/main`, but between it and main the gradient-bearing files moved **1,032 insertions / 297 deletions**, **673 lines of that in `autograd.py` itself**, and nothing has re-scored the whole-model per-parameter claim since. **What DOES cover main exactly is the op-level gate, and the bridge had to be REBUILT this pass because the published one had silently collapsed**. It named `f0e8f3b71`; between that tree and today's `origin/main` `a1c35618e`, `autograd.py` and `taped_ttnn.py` moved **168 insertions / 54 deletions** through this sprint's own `of3t-softbw` and `of3t-wheelbw` merges (`456f98e76`, `4a61ac332`, 2026-09-25 22:02), so the byte-identity the claim rested on is **false as published** — three of the five files still match, two do not. The replacement is two hours old and stronger: `of3t-innercfg` ran `batch_gate.sh` **rc 0, 16/16** at `rel_l2 <= 1.0e-02` against float64 references each validated by central finite differences, with all three controls firing, on `origin/main` `91532cc9b` plus nine comment lines proven inert by `ast.dump` equality — and all five of `tt_bio/{autograd,taped_ttnn,tenstorrent,openfold3_trunk,openfold3_data}.py` are **byte-identical by blob hash** between `91532cc9b` and `a1c35618e`, the only `tt_bio/` change between them being **29 lines of docstring** in `size_limits.py`'s ceilings table. A bridge to main is a perishable claim and nothing was re-checking it. A per-op gate and a per-parameter model score are different instruments, so the byte-identity does not extend the section-level or coverage claims. **Re-scoring on current main is owed, and the published artifact now SAYS SO ITSELF (R255).** Regenerated this pass from `origin/main` against a tree that exists: **5 of 5 MET, `n_stale` 5**, break controls green, spec `b8874583f28b` equal to the gate's, each shortfall published — GRADIENTS **>=33.5 h**, DRAWS 20.0, SECTIONS 20.4, TRAJECTORY **86.7**, COVERAGE **>=150.5 h** (dated by its oldest source, K55). It also now records **`tree_commit` `cdd2c2f38`**, verified an ancestor of main, because the previous copy named a worktree deleted days earlier. **(K53, corrected pass 500.)** `charter_evidence.py` does have expiry checking — `code_staleness()` at line 132, called per condition — and in the live `CHARTER_EVIDENCE.json` it reads `artifact_is_older_than_code: true` on **all five**. Corrected figures after K55 re-dated composed artifacts by their sources: GRADIENTS **>=31.7 h**, DRAWS 18.3, SECTIONS 18.7, TRAJECTORY **85.0**, COVERAGE **>=148.8 h** — COVERAGE was reading 17.8 h because the gate dated the merge rather than its six-day-old census (8.4x, in the flattering direction). The instrument was right; `main()` printed only `5 of 5 met` and the qualifier stayed in the JSON. **Fixed**: each condition prints `STALE by >= N h`, the headline says the count may not be quoted without it, and the payload carries `n_stale` / `n_unreadable`. Still non-failing, because re-taking an artifact needs a card. **The `>=` is exact rather than hedged (K54): this dates the artifact's COMMIT, and an artifact is measured before it is committed, so the figure is a lower bound.** The sibling instrument `baseline_expiry.py` dates by self-recorded `env.commit` and is **correctly UNDATABLE on all five — none of them carries an `env` block at all**, verified by reading them this pass. Two methods, opposite readings, both right; the producer-side fix is to record `env.commit`, which means re-taking them, which needs a card. **So the honest statement is: 5 of 5 MET, all five graded on artifacts at least 18.3 to 148.8 hours older than the code, with 24 commits to `autograd.py` since the stamp `f01fa0813`.** Closing it means re-deriving 4,152 tensors against the float64 reference on main, which the scoring arm cannot do. GRADIENT-CONFIDENCE: Confident, and verified rather than inferred: OpenFold3's training gradient on Tenstorrent is upstream 0.4.3's gradient to within upstream's own bf16 error, on every section, over the whole step. It rests on the four fields below, each read off its artifact by `perf/of3t_orchestrator/charter/charter_evidence.py` into `state/of3t/CHARTER_EVIDENCE.json` (5 of 5 MET, spec sha `b8874583f28b` equal to this gate's, break control green), on `wk/of3t` `f01fa0813`.

GRADIENTS: Whole-model, every parameter: 4152 tensors of the full training step (trunk, diffusion, distogram, confidence heads), one 384-wide denoise step, scored per tensor by `perf/of3t_fullstep64/score.py` against the A40-validated float64 reference with upstream's own bf16 step as the bar (`perf/of3t_paedraws/SCORE_PD384.json`). 0 unread, 0 placed-but-carried-nothing, 0 multi-placed; global rel 1.55834e-01 against bf16's 9.48232e-01; 98.07 % of the float64 mass at or better than bf16 on draw 0 and 99.13 % on the six-draw mean (A45, `perf/of3t_orchestrator/a45/DRAWS_A45.json`). Worst systematic case: `aux_heads.distogram.linear.weight` at 1.44x its bf16 on every draw (D270, 0.857 % of mass), inside the 3x section bar; all 21 of 21 sections within 3x (`SECTIONS_PD384.json`).

TRAJECTORY: 20 steps, coupled, whole model covering 89.2106 % of its squared gradient norm (`perf/of3t_trajfull/traj_trajfull.json`); upstream's weights move at 19 of 20 steps and ours at all 20. Operating point stated in the artifact: the LR ramp reaches 11.4 % of peak and the clip coefficient is 1.0 throughout, so the knee, the decay and an active clip are driven by the state-free factor checks in PROTOCOL, not by this run.

COVERAGE: All 8 of upstream's LossWeights terms and all 11 conditional paths fire at runtime on the batch, each with the stage and dataset that carried it (`perf/of3t_orchestrator/coverage/COVERAGE_MERGED.json`).
DOESNOT: **This proves the UPDATE RULE over N steps. It does not prove stability over a full
training run**, and no artifact of this campaign may be described as one. Specifically not proven:
behaviour over 100k steps, precision drift accumulating across a long run, rare sample types the
batch never contained, and convergence to upstream's published weights. The honest sentence is
*"our training step is their training step, verified per-parameter with full path coverage"*.

**And the sprint's own bound, stated before its first number exists.** A speed result says seconds
off one crop-384 step on one board at one clock. It says nothing about a long run's throughput
until `of3t-throughput` supplies the samples/sec axis, and a per-step win does not compose into a
time-to-model claim by arithmetic — the host share is real and this campaign already measured a
sibling case where 79.2 % of a round was host work the port never covered, capping every credited
lever at 1.25x. Stack perturbations are strongly sub-additive, so the sprint's levers are approved
as a stack or not at all, never by summing individual readings.

GAP: **Pass 537. Current state, replacing pass 497's, which was a running log of a board that is now empty.**

1. **The per-parameter model-scope score has not been re-taken on main, and that is the one real
   hole.** The 4,152-tensor whole-step comparison against the A40-validated float64 reference was
   taken on `f01fa0813`; `autograd.py` has moved 24 commits since. What covers today's main is the
   **op-level** gate — `batch_gate.sh` 16/16 on a tree byte-identical to `a1c35618e` on all five
   gradient-bearing files (see PROVES). A per-op gate and a per-parameter model score are different
   instruments and the byte-identity does not promote one into the other. Re-taking it means
   re-deriving 4,152 tensors against the float64 reference on a card, roughly 33 h of arm time, and
   pc cannot run the crop-384 exactness-ON step at all — `of3t-stepqb1` showed the in-flight
   float64 working set of one exact-softmax backward needs **>=17.3185 GiB** against a 26.5 GiB box
   with ~108 backwards ahead of it. So this is a cost, not a mystery, and it is priced.

2. **All five charter conditions are graded on artifacts older than the code they grade.**
   `CHARTER_EVIDENCE.json` reads 5 of 5 MET with `n_stale` **5** and publishes each shortfall:
   GRADIENTS **>=31.7 h**, DRAWS 18.3, SECTIONS 18.7, TRAJECTORY **85.0**, COVERAGE **>=148.8 h**.
   The `>=` is exact rather than hedged (K54) — it dates the artifact's commit and an artifact is
   measured before it is committed. Non-failing by design, because re-taking any of them needs a
   card. The count may not be quoted without the staleness, and `charter_evidence.py` now prints
   them together so it cannot be.

3. **Three user-facing defects are carried, not closed: D184, D210, D250.** Each is a decision
   already taken and written down — a lever NO-GO'd on measurement, another campaign's release
   item, and a lever Moritz's 2026-09-21 constraint holds off default. Ask 10455 decided on
   2026-09-24 that GO rides on gradients and carries these as separately owned. They belong to
   whoever owns defect closure; this campaign is not the right owner for any of the three.

4. **The backward sprint's own answer bounds what a successor should try.** The backward is
   **663.3 s**, of which **73.5 % of verb time is host crossings** (`to_torch` 178.41 +
   `from_torch` 139.13 = 317.54 s) against under 2 s of the model's own arithmetic and `matmul` at
   0.85 s over 4,672 calls. The fused-backward-kernel programme is refuted (J1 NO-GO, J2's free
   route NO-GO, J3 dead at zero, the taped bypass 1.005x), and `of3t-xroof` found **86 s** of the
   crossing (165.99 → 80.2 s) by shrinking the step's host memory rather than by reserving the box.
   The remaining crossing is not a board roof: `to_device` runs at **14.20 GB/s = 90.2 %** of Gen4
   x8's raw 15.75, and the binding term is the **host tile-shuffle** (untilize 4.13 / tilize 6.59
   against a warm `copy_` at 36.9). Every banked `gb_s` figure in this campaign is **void** — R245
   found `bwprof.py`'s `gb` column billing both ends of each crossing and undersizing fp32 2x — and
   every seconds column stands.

5. **pc sits at 3 of 4 hugepages because of me.** `state/pc-hugepages-degraded` records it. Usable
   28.502 GiB against the vendor default's 26.502; the in-use page was never touched and the live
   arm stayed healthy through the change. Whoever next tunes that box should know it was a
   deliberate reservation, not drift.

VERDICT: GO, pass 537 — the charter is met, carrying D184, D210 and D250 as separately owned under ask 10455's 2026-09-24 decision, and the campaign concludes.

**What GO means here, in one sentence:** we are confident OpenFold3's training gradient on
Tenstorrent is upstream 0.4.3's gradient to within upstream's own bf16 error, per parameter, over
the whole step, with every loss term and conditional path shown to fire — and the confidence rests
on five artifact-graded conditions plus an op-level gate that reaches today's main, with the two
things it does **not** establish written in DOESNOT and GAP rather than left to be inferred.

**Three things changed this pass and each of them mattered.**

**1. D55 closed, 4 → 3.** `of3t-innercfg` reported, on the condition pass 528 fixed in advance.
The answer was zero in two independent senses — `ttnn.sum` already accumulates in fp32, so the
missing kwarg is bit-identical out to 6.35 cancelled digits; and under the shipped default the line
fires **0 times** on the OF3 trunk at any crop, which refutes the filing's own premise. The row
landed no code change and was right not to: a provably no-op edit in a file contested with BCX is a
merge hazard bought for nothing, and it proved the inertness with `ast.dump` equality against main
rather than arguing it. **A defect can close on a measurement that says the defect was never on the
path it was filed against.**

**2. The bridge from the gradient claim to `main` had collapsed and nothing was watching it.** The
published claim named `f0e8f3b71` and asserted byte-identity on five files. Checked this pass
against `origin/main` `a1c35618e`: two of the five have moved, **168 insertions / 54 deletions** in
`autograd.py` and `taped_ttnn.py`, through this sprint's own `of3t-softbw` and `of3t-wheelbw`
merges at 22:02 last night. Had I stamped GO on the doc as written I would have stamped it on a
sentence that was false. The replacement is two hours old and stronger — `of3t-innercfg`'s
`batch_gate.sh` rc 0, 16/16 at `rel_l2 <= 1.0e-02` with FD-validated float64 references and all
three controls firing, on a tree byte-identical to `a1c35618e` on all five files, the only `tt_bio/`
difference being 29 lines of docstring. **A byte-identity bridge is a perishable claim and needs
re-checking on the pass that uses it, not on the pass that wrote it.**

**3. The clause that blocked GO for five passes had an answer two days older than the block.** The
gate refuses GO while a defect is USER-FACING — and carries a carve-out for the ids ask 10455 names
and the VERDICT line names, which is Moritz's own recorded decision to GO on gradients and carry
the non-gradient items. I read the clause and stopped at the refusal. Five passes, a terminal
condition written into this doc committing the campaign to a verdict its own gate structurally
refuses, and a dispatched row held as the excuse. **When a gate refuses you repeatedly, read its
carve-outs before writing a terminal condition around it** — the asymmetry is that the refusal is
loud and the exemption is silent.

**The sprint's own question stays answered and unflattering**: the backward is slow because of the
fidelity we chose, not a missing kernel. 663.3 s, 73.5 % of verb time in host crossings, the model's
arithmetic under 2 s, the fused-kernel programme refuted on four counts, and the remaining crossing
bound by the host tile-shuffle rather than by the board. EXIT 5 of 5, every item closed on a
condition written before the result that closed it.

**Not carried forward as a win:** the whole-model per-parameter re-score on current main. It is
owed, it is priced at ~33 h of card time, and pc physically cannot run the arm. GAP item 1.
